articles.title: Goldman Sachs: The FOMC - FJElite
articles.expand: The FOMC raised the funds rate by 25bp to 3.75-4% today. While the hike was widely expected, the meeting was more hawkish than we expected in a few ways. First, a 16-2 majority projected at least one more hike this year, and there were no dissenting votes against today’s hike. Second, the median funds rate projection remained quite elevated through 2029, and the median neutral rate dot rose from 3.06% to 3.25%. articles.title: BoE preview: Bank Rate seen on hold as Iran-driven energy shock stirs hike talk
articles.expand: The story here is energy, not the rate decision itself. British natural gas and Brent crude have jumped nearly 20% this month on the back of the Iran war, the same driver that pushed the Fed to hike a day earlier and has already moved the ECB. That leaves sterling and UK rates markets more exposed to the path of oil and gas prices than to Thursday's widely expected hold , since a further leg up in energy costs would strengthen the case for the November hike markets are already pricing at 80%. articles.title: The Riksbank’s Business Survey: “There was some concern before the summer, but then things took a turn for the better”
articles.expand: The economic situation has improved since last spring and, for the first time since September 2022, large Swedish companies’ assessment of the situation is now above its historical average. Before the summer, there were fears that the war in the Middle East would delay the recovery, but those fears have not materialised. Demand has strengthened and the cost increases resulting from the war are considered to be manageable. As a result, companies are taking a more optimistic view of future developments. This is revealed by the Riksbank’s Business Survey in August.
